title: The adjoint scheme-module pullback is strong monoidal
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. On the categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], equip both sides with the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The Mathlib functor Scheme.Modules.pullback f, defined as the left adjoint of the module pushforward along f, has a strong monoidal structure: its unit and tensor comparison maps are isomorphisms, natural in the modules, satisfying the associativity and unit diagrams.

proof.text: Use the already proved source-library instance Scheme.Modules.pullbackMonoidal. Its construction equips the presheaf pullback followed by sheafification with the composite monoidal structure. The natural isomorphism SheafOfModules.sheafificationCompPullback identifies this composite with sheafification followed by module pullback. Sheafification is a monoidal localization, and Localization.Monoidal.functorMonoidalOfComp descends the composite structure to the sheaf pullback. The descended structure includes invertible unit and tensorators and their naturality, associativity and unit laws. This is the actual definition of the recorded instance, not an additional proof obligation.
